negative_reviews.author: The Scottish Guide
negative_reviews.text:
The food at Maki & Ramen was lovely as always, but unfortunately the customer service really let the experience down.

From the moment we walked in, the young lady serving us was cold, dismissive and unwelcoming. Despite several interactions, there was very little in the way of basic manners or friendliness. We also noticed the same attitude towards other customers.

It's a real shame as the food has always been excellent, but good customer service is just as important. Having a service charge added to the bill after such poor service was particularly disappointing.

Looking at other reviews, it seems we're not the only ones to have experienced this. Hopefully management takes the feedback on board, as the service really needs improving.

negative_reviews.author: Zakariyya Majid
negative_reviews.text:
I visited with a friend, and the ramen was terrific. Best in the city. However, the experience was let down by really really poor service.

The interaction felt rather cold from the outset, there was little warmth or friendliness, and we were sat down with barely a word spoken, and the server never returned. We needed multiple attempts to get her attention, as we were ready to order.

Once the food arrived, we had to make several more attempts to get the server’s attention when we needed extra cutlery, and at no point during the meal were we checked on or asked if everything was okay. It felt dismissive, however we also noticed the same attitude towards other customers, unfortunately.

And on top of the two £17 ramen bowls, we ended up paying a £3.50 service charge, so I was left disappointed with what we received in return for the additional charge, instead of the fantastic ramen we’d just eaten.

Unfortunately I am disappointed about my visit.
The biggest compliment goes to hard working staff, who managed to work fast, be kind and polite during a very busy evening period.
We were sat on a table that’s in between of everything. Every minute there were staff members or other customers walking around us. Tables are tiny and I had to put my handbag on the floor, as there wouldn’t be space for it on the table.
The ramen itself was underwhelming. Probably the most mid ramen I’ve ever had. It came lukewarm at best. Chashu pork should had been grilled for a longer time and had an unpleasant smell. It wasn’t bad, but there are so many better ramen shops in Soho.
It’s the first time in my life when I had a starter, ramen and a drink and I didn’t leave feeling very full.
Prices are good, and bubble tea was tasty (but it’s a small glass with a lot of ice in it).
The last disappointment was music - we expected Japanese music, but instead they play American and English pop.

negative_reviews.author: frank
negative_reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing

I’ve visited multiple Maki & Ramen locations across London and have never had a bad experience. Unfortunately, the Southampton location was an entirely different story.

I visited last Thursday and, despite the restaurant being extremely quiet (no more than five tables occupied), we waited at least 10 minutes just to be seated.It took a further 25 minutes for a member of staff to come and take our drink order, despite us watching them serve tables who had arrived after us. Whether this was because we are young or simply a lack of organisation and proper order of service, I couldn’t say.

Initially, we only ordered soft drinks, which took so long to arrive that our food order had already been taken by the time they reached the table.

We opted for the £18 lunch deal, upgrading a few items, which would have been great value for money had the food been of an acceptable standard.

We started with the chicken gyozas, which were extremely bland and genuinely some of the worst I’ve had in a restaurant. We also upgraded to the dynamite prawns, which I’ve previously eaten at the Soho location. However, these were equally disappointing, with virtually no spice and very little sauce.

For mains, we chose the chicken yakisoba, which was okay, and upgraded to the steak ramen, which was frankly appalling. The broth had a very unpleasant aftertaste and the steak was entirely grey. We also ordered the rainbow sushi roll, another dish I’d previously enjoyed at the Soho location. Whilst most of the roll was delicious, the sea bream had an unusually strong fishy smell and didn’t taste right.

Throughout the meal, not a single member of staff came over to check whether everything was okay. Had anyone bothered to do so, we would have raised our concerns and sent back both the ramen and the sushi.

We also upgraded our drinks to a Pornstar Martini and a Gaia cocktail. Whilst there was nothing particularly wrong with the taste, both arrived halfway through our meal and were practically dumped on the table.

To top it all off, a service charge was automatically added to the bill, which felt particularly insulting given the standard of service we’d received.

Shortly after leaving the restaurant, we both became extremely unwell with symptoms consistent with food poisoning. I cannot say with certainty which dish, if any, was responsible, but the timing was concerning, particularly given our experience with the steak ramen and the fish in the sushi.

Having previously had such positive experiences at other Maki & Ramen locations, this visit was incredibly disappointing. The service was unacceptable, the food quality was inconsistent at best, and the experience as a whole has completely put me off returning to the Southampton branch. I would strongly encourage others to think twice before visiting.
